subject: accountancy

bankRead: Saved read-only snapshot of 20 Nov 2026 (scratchpad accB: bank_accountancy.json 1,515 rows, served_accountancy.json 1,179 served ids, suspended.json empty). No database access in this run.
keyCardDeck: data/keycards/decks/accountancy.json (1,127 cards, none suspended in the snapshot)
syllabusSource: data/canonical_syllabus.js plus the CUET 2026 Accountancy syllabus text (data/source_registry.json, cuet2026-accountancy-syllabus); every question sits on the 2026 syllabus
method: tmp/1120-speed/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; doubtful = not covered; numericals need a served bank question with the same steps; Key cards count for theory). Facts written first in coverage/acc26_facts.mjs; searches with acc26_search.mjs and acc26_templates.mjs.
paperStructure: Core 45 (all compulsory) + one optional Part of 5: Analysis of Financial Statements or Computerized Accounting Systems. A candidate answers 50.

facts: In the absence of a partnership deed no interest on capital is allowed (Partnership Act default rules)

matches.teaches: When the deed is silent, no interest on capital is allowed

questions.reason: Key card states that with no deed (deed silent) no interest on capital is allowed.

facts: Under the fixed capital method, salary to a partner is credited to the partner's current account

matches.teaches: Fixed capital: drawings, salary, interest on capital are posted to current accounts

questions.reason: Key card states that under fixed capitals salary is posted to the current account.

facts: Interest on capital: opening capital for the full year, additional capital from the date introduced, and capital withdrawn reduced from the date of withdrawal (time-weighted, months)
questions.reason: The served bank only has full-year interest on a single opening capital (138 templated rows like 00e30f6f); no served question time-weights additional capital and a withdrawal.

facts: When the deed allows interest on capital but the profit is less than the total interest, the profit is shared in the ratio of interest on capital (capital ratio), so the partner gets less than full interest
questions.reason: Served appropriation numericals (7f24b118, b41fb23e) all have enough profit; none shares an insufficient profit in the ratio of interest on capital.

facts: Partnership arises from an agreement between partners
Sharing of profits (and losses) of a business is an essential feature
Mutual agency: each partner is principal and agent for the others
Mere co-ownership of property does not amount to partnership (not an essential feature)

matches.teaches: Essential features: agreement, business, mutual agency, sharing of profit (two or more persons, liability)
Mere co-ownership of property does not amount to partnership
Each partner is principal as well as agent for the others

questions.reason: All four statements taught on Key cards, including that co-ownership is not partnership.

facts: If nothing is specified, the new partner is assumed to acquire his share from the old partners in their old profit sharing ratio (sacrificing ratio equals the old ratio)

matches.teaches: If nothing is specified the new partner gets his share from old partners in their profit sharing ratio
A and B 3:2 admit C for 1/5: sacrifice ratio 3:2 (the old ratio)

questions.reason: Key card carries the exact sentence; bank question shows the sacrifice ratio equals the old ratio.

facts: Under the Partnership Act 1932 a new partner can be admitted only with the consent of all existing partners, unless otherwise agreed

matches.teaches: New partner admitted only with consent of all existing partners (Partnership Act 1932)

questions.reason: Key card carries the exact rule.

facts: In the absence of information, remaining partners acquire the retiring partner's share in their old profit sharing ratio (gaining ratio equals the old ratio)

matches.teaches: With no information, continuing partners acquire the outgoing partner's share in the old ratio

questions.reason: Key card states the assumption exactly.

facts: The ratio in which continuing partners acquire the deceased (or retiring) partner's share is the gaining ratio

matches.teaches: Statement II correct: gaining ratio is the ratio in which continuing partners acquire the share of a retiring partner
Ratio in which continuing partners acquire the retiring/deceased partner's share = gaining ratio

questions.reason: Key card defines it with the retiring/deceased wording; the bank question teaches it for retirement.

facts: At retirement, accumulated profits or losses (reserves) belong to all the partners (including the retiring one) and are distributed in the old ratio

matches.teaches: Accumulated profits or losses belong to all the partners (old ratio)

questions.reason: Key card states they belong to all the partners.

facts: Gaining ratio and new ratio are determined first (they govern goodwill adjustment)
Revaluation account is prepared and its profit or loss is transferred to the partners' capital accounts, including the deceased partner's
The balance of the deceased partner's capital account is transferred to his executor's account (executor's account comes last)

matches.teaches: Order of aspects: 1 new ratio and gaining ratio, 3 revaluation, 8 settlement of amounts due
Revaluation result goes to all partners' capital accounts including the deceased partner's
Amount credited to a deceased partner is transferred to his Executors' Account

questions.reason: Cards give gaining ratio first, revaluation to capital accounts, then the executor's account; every step taught.

facts: Debit balance of the retiring partner's current account is deducted from his dues
Share of goodwill written off (existing goodwill written off) is deducted
Share of accumulated losses is deducted
Share of loss on revaluation is deducted

matches.teaches: Deductions: debit balance of current account, goodwill written off, accumulated losses, revaluation loss

questions.reason: Key card lists all four deductions.

facts: Revaluation account is prepared first at retirement
Partners' current account balances are transferred to (or adjusted through) partners' capital accounts, so current accounts come before capital accounts
The balance sheet of the reconstituted firm is prepared last
questions.reason: Revaluation account and balance sheet are taught, but no served material orders partners' current accounts before capital accounts at retirement, which the key tests.

facts: Gaining ratio = New ratio - Old ratio
Sacrificing ratio = Old ratio - New ratio
Goodwill by capitalisation of super profit = Super profit x 100 / Normal rate of return
Capitalised value of average profit = Average profit x 100 / Normal rate of return

matches.teaches: Gaining share = New share - Old share
Sacrifice = Old share - New share
Goodwill = Super profits x 100 / Normal rate of return
Capitalised value of average profits = Average profits x 100 / Normal rate of return

questions.reason: All four formulas are on Key cards.

facts: AS 26 is the Accounting Standard that deals with (defines) intangible assets
questions.reason: AS 26 is mentioned only on card goodwill-valuation.fact-internal-goodwill-not-recognised, which never says AS 26 is the standard on intangible assets.

facts: Reverse super profit method: super profit = goodwill / years of purchase; normal profit = average profit - super profit; normal rate of return = normal profit / capital employed x 100 (unknown: the normal rate)
questions.reason: Served goodwill numericals (80a94a54, 9660cdbd) go forward to goodwill; none works back from goodwill to the normal rate of return.

facts: Profit to the date of death on the sales basis: last year's profit / last year's sales x sales up to the date of death (the firm's profit, not the partner's share)
questions.reason: No served question computes profit to the date of death on the sales (turnover) basis; 212dadfc uses the time basis.

facts: Revaluation profit or loss = total increases in asset values - total decreases (here gains and losses cancel to nil)
questions.reason: No served question computes a net revaluation profit or loss from several asset revaluations (c4c9ea99 only splits a given loss).

facts: When the new partner cannot bring his share of goodwill in cash, his current (or capital) account is debited with his share of goodwill
The credit goes to the sacrificing (old) partners' capital accounts in the sacrificing ratio (here the old ratio 3:2)

matches.teaches: Incoming Partner's Current A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partners' Capital A/cs (goodwill not brought)
Sacrifice in the old ratio when nothing is specified (9,000 : 6,000)

questions.reason: Key card gives the keyed entry exactly: new partner's current account debited, sacrificing partners credited.

facts: Self-generated goodwill is not recorded in the books as an asset (only purchased goodwill is)

matches.teaches: Under AS 26, internally generated goodwill should not be recognised as an asset

questions.reason: Key card: self-generated (internally generated) goodwill is not recognised as an asset.

facts: Intangible assets are written off over their estimated life, not exceeding 10 years (AS 26)
AS 26 deals with intangible assets
Section 37 of the Partnership Act: the retiring partner's option of interest @6% p.a. or a share of profits earned with his money
Section 4 of the Partnership Act defines partnership

matches.teaches: Section 4 defines partnership
Section 37: interest @6% or share of profits to the outgoing partner

questions.reason: Two of four pairs taught (Section 4, Section 37); the 10-year write-off of intangibles and "AS 26 deals with intangible assets" are taught nowhere.

facts: Sacrificing ratio when old partners' mutual new ratio is given: new shares = remaining share (1 - new partner's share) x given ratio; sacrifice = old share - new share; ratio of sacrifices
questions.reason: Served admission numericals (20fa6daa, 7c532466) keep the old ratio; none gives the old partners a new mutual ratio and works out the sacrifice from it.

facts: Super profit method with partners' salary: adjust past profits by deducting partners' remuneration, average them, deduct normal profit (capital x normal rate), multiply super profit by years of purchase
questions.reason: Forward super profit is served (9660cdbd), but no served question deducts partners' salary from past profits and averages them before the super profit step.

facts: Profit and Loss Suspense Account (credited to the deceased partner for his share of profit to date of death) is later closed by debiting the gaining partners' capital accounts (NTA key)

matches.teaches: Gaining Partners Capital A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss Suspense A/c (on death)
Gaining Partners Capital A/c Dr. (gaining ratio) To P&L Suspense A/c

questions.reason: Key card gives the keyed closing entry exactly.

facts: Accumulated loss (debit balance of Profit and Loss Account) at admission is written off to old partners' capital accounts in the old ratio: Old Partners' Capital A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c

matches.teaches: Debit balance of P&L A/c at admission is transferred to old partners' capital accounts
Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c

questions.reason: Key cards give the rule and the entry.

facts: Perpetual succession: a company continues to exist whatever happens to its members (members come and go)

matches.teaches: Company continues to exist irrespective of changes in its membership

questions.reason: Key card defines perpetual succession in the same terms.

facts: One Person Company limit (Rule 3, Companies (Incorporation) Rules 2014): average annual turnover of three years not exceeding Rs 2 crore

matches.teaches: OPC: paid-up capital not over Rs 50 lakh, average annual turnover of three years not over Rs 2 crore

questions.reason: Key card states the Rs 2 crore turnover limit.

facts: Equity shareholders are entitled to the remaining (distributable) profits after the preference dividend is paid

matches.teaches: Equity shareholders share distributable profits after preference dividend rights

questions.reason: Key card carries the exact sentence.

facts: Minimum subscription under SEBI guidelines is 90% of the issued amount

matches.teaches: Minimum subscription under SEBI guidelines: 90% of the issue
Minimum subscription cannot be less than 90% of the issued amount (SEBI DIP Guidelines 2000)

questions.reason: Same fact asked directly in a served bank question; also on a Key card.

facts: A debenture is a written instrument acknowledging a debt under the company's common seal

matches.teaches: Debenture is a written instrument acknowledging a debt under the common seal of the company

questions.reason: Key card definition word for word.

facts: On bearer debentures interest is paid to whoever produces the interest coupon attached to the debenture

matches.teaches: Interest is paid to a person who produces the interest coupon attached

questions.reason: Key card carries the exact sentence.

facts: Debentures for consideration other than cash: assets bought from vendors and paid for by debentures
Debentures as collateral security: issued to lenders in addition to other assets already pledged
Debentures for cash: the public is invited to apply through a prospectus
Debentures at discount: issued at a price lower than face value

matches.teaches: Debentures issued to vendors/suppliers without receiving cash
Own debentures issued to lenders in addition to other assets already pledged
Debentures (for cash) are offered to the public and applied for
Prospectus is an invitation to the public for funds
Issued at a price below nominal value = at a discount

questions.reason: All four pairs taught on Key cards; the cash issue through public applications is taught by the over-subscription and prospectus cards.

facts: Securities premium may be used to write off preliminary expenses
Securities premium may be used to pay premium on redemption of preference shares or debentures
Securities premium may be used to write off expenses of, commission paid or discount allowed on issue of securities
Securities premium may NOT be used to pay the issue price of debentures (not a permitted use under Section 52)

matches.teaches: Securities premium can be used only for 5 purposes: bonus shares, preliminary expenses, issue expenses/commission/discount, premium on redemption, buy-back
Securities premium can be used to write off preliminary expenses

questions.reason: Key card lists the only permitted uses: A, B and C are on it, paying the issue price of debentures is not.

facts: Calls in arrears (non-payment) come first and lead to forfeiture
Forfeited shares may then be reissued
After reissue, the remaining balance of the share forfeited account is transferred to capital reserve

matches.teaches: Shares forfeited when allotment or call money is unpaid
Reissue of forfeited shares
Balance of forfeited account on reissued shares transferred to capital reserve
Profit on reissue of forfeited shares goes to Capital Reserve

questions.reason: Unpaid calls lead to forfeiture, then reissue, then transfer to capital reserve: every step taught.

facts: Shares issued for consideration other than cash at a premium: number of shares = amount to be paid in shares (price less cash paid) / issue price (face value + premium)
questions.reason: No served question finds the number of shares issued to a vendor at a premium (e447dd1e is at par and gives the number).

facts: Debentures issued to a vendor at a discount: number = amount payable / issue price (face - discount); entry Vendor Dr (amount) + Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr (discount) To Debentures (face value)
questions.reason: No served bank question issues debentures to a vendor at a discount; card debentures.entry-vendor-at-discount gives the entry only, which does not count for a numerical.

facts: Debentures issued at a premium payable in instalments: application, allotment (including premium: credit Debentures and Securities Premium separately) and call entries with the right amounts (number x per-debenture amount)
questions.reason: Served debenture numericals are one template (00c334d1, issue at a discount); none has debentures at a premium payable in instalments.

facts: On repayment of the loan, debentures issued as collateral security are cancelled by reversing the original entry: Debentures A/c Dr. To Debenture Suspense A/c

matches.teaches: On repayment: Debentures A/c Dr. To Debenture Suspense A/c

questions.reason: Key card gives the keyed cancellation entry.

facts: Nominal (authorised) share capital is the maximum share capital a company is authorised to issue

matches.teaches: Authorised capital is the maximum the company may issue, also called nominal capital

questions.reason: Key card defines authorised capital and says it is also called nominal capital.

facts: Forfeiture when allotment money including premium is unpaid: premium not received is not credited to forfeiture; amount forfeited = amount received on capital; capital reserve = amount forfeited - discount on reissue (here nil)
questions.reason: Served forfeiture-reissue numericals (13586296) are at par; none excludes unpaid premium from the forfeited amount, which is the step the key turns on.

facts: A firm formed for a particular venture is dissolved on completion of that venture: dissolution on the happening of certain contingencies (Section 42)

matches.teaches: Firm constituted for a venture is dissolved on its completion (contingency)

questions.reason: Key card lists completion of the venture as a contingency.

facts: Court may dissolve a firm when a partner persistently breaches the partnership agreement
Court may dissolve a firm when a partner transfers the whole of his interest to a third party
Court may dissolve a firm when the business cannot be carried on except at a loss
Death of a partner dissolves the firm on a contingency, not by court order

matches.teaches: Court grounds include persistent breach, transfer of whole interest, business only at a loss
Death of a partner is a contingency, not a court ground

questions.reason: Cards give the court grounds A, B, D and place death among contingencies.

facts: Outside creditors (liabilities) are paid first
Partners' loans are paid next, before capitals
Partners' capitals are then paid
Any surplus left is distributed among partners in the profit sharing ratio

matches.teaches: Third-party debts, then partners' loans, then capitals, then residue in profit sharing ratio
Outside liabilities first, then partners' loans, then capitals

questions.reason: Key card gives the full Section 48 order.

facts: Realisation expenses paid by the firm: Realisation A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
Paid by a partner on behalf of the firm: Realisation A/c Dr. To Partner's Capital A/c
A partner bears the expenses but the firm pays: Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
A partner bears and pays the expenses himself: no entry in the firm's books

matches.teaches: Realisation A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
Realisation A/c Dr. To Partner's Capital A/c
Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
No entry is required

questions.reason: One Key card per case; all four taught.

facts: Cash realised from an asset when part is taken over by a partner (no cash) and the rest is sold at a gain: cash = (book value of the part sold) x (1 + gain %)
questions.reason: No served question works out the cash realised when a partner takes over part of an asset and the rest is sold at a gain (bb96a884 is a realisation-account effect only).

facts: Receipts from royalties, fees, commission and other revenue are operating activities
Receipt of interest and dividends is an investing activity (non-financial enterprise)
Proceeds from issue of equity or preference shares are financing activities
Current investments (short-term, readily convertible) are cash equivalents

matches.teaches: Receipts from royalties, fees, commissions and other revenues are operating
Receipt of interest and dividends is investing (non-financial enterprise)
Proceeds from issuing equity or preference shares are financing
Short-term investments that are cash equivalents

questions.reason: All four pairs on Key cards.

facts: The statement of profit and loss begins with revenue from operations
Expenses such as cost of materials consumed come next
Profit before exceptional and extraordinary items and tax comes before profit before tax

matches.teaches: I Revenue from operations comes first
Cost of materials consumed is an expense item (IV)
VII Profit before extraordinary items and tax, then IX Profit before tax

questions.reason: Key cards give the Schedule III order with item numbers.

facts: When the current ratio is above 1, an equal increase in current assets and current liabilities (credit purchase of goods) reduces the current ratio

matches.teaches: Current ratio 2:1, goods bought on credit: ratio falls to 1.7:1, reduced

questions.reason: Key card works this exact case; it asks the direction, not a computation.

facts: Interest coverage ratio = profit before interest and tax / interest; PBT = PAT / (1 - tax rate); interest = rate x long-term debt; EBIT = PBT + interest
questions.reason: The served bank has no interest coverage ratio question at all.

facts: Comparative statements are called horizontal analysis

matches.teaches: Comparative statements analysis is also known as 'horizontal analysis'

questions.reason: Key card states it exactly.

facts: Advantages of CAS include timely generation of reports and information in the desired format
Advantages include efficient record keeping
Advantages include effective control over the system
CAS brings economy in processing accounting data (it is an advantage, so "economy is minimised" is not one)

matches.teaches: Advantages: timely reports, efficient record keeping, effective control, economy in processing, confidentiality

questions.reason: Key card lists all four advantages in the same words; "economy is minimised" is the distortion.

facts: A range is identified by the references of its upper-left and lower-right cells
A mixed reference holds either the row or the column constant when copied
An absolute reference stays fixed on a specific cell
The default (relative) reference changes to reflect the new location when copied

matches.teaches: Ranges identified by start and end cells, e.g. A1:E2
Mixed reference holds row or column constant
Absolute reference stays fixed on a specific cell
By default references are relative and change when copied

questions.reason: All four pairs on Key cards.

facts: Select the cell(s) containing the formula first
Copy them
Choose Paste Special
Select Values and click OK (freezes the formula as values)
questions.reason: No served material teaches the Paste Special > Values steps.

facts: In spreadsheet financial functions, Nper is the total number of payment periods

matches.teaches: Nper: total number of payments for the loan

questions.reason: Key card defines Nper exactly.

facts: A graph (chart) has at least two axes (horizontal x and vertical y)

matches.teaches: A graph has at least two axes, X and Y

questions.reason: Key card carries the exact fact.
